title: Pan American Fire & Casualty Co. v. Revere (1960)
summary: The insurer could invoke interpleader before the accident claimants reduced their demands to judgments.
notes:
Read the scope of the injunction alongside State Farm v. Tashire. Interpleader over insurance money does not automatically authorize control of every related tort action.

The case arose in the Eastern District of Louisiana (Judge J. Skelly Wright) from a collision between a tractor-trailer and a school bus near Covington, Louisiana; the insurer deposited a $100,000 bond equal to its policy limit, and the court enjoined all claimants from suing elsewhere, required claims to be filed within 30 days, and ordered a joint trial on liability and damages.

sections.Parties: An insurer faced numerous claims arising from a collision involving a tractor-trailer and a bus.
sections.Material Facts: The accident caused deaths and injuries, producing claims that could exceed the policy’s limited coverage. The claims were not yet reduced to judgments, and the potential claimants were dispersed. The insurer sought a single proceeding concerning the available insurance money.
sections.Procedural History: The federal court considered whether the unliquidated claims and the insurer’s continuing obligations barred interpleader. It permitted interpleader while addressing the limits of relief and the insurer’s obligations.
sections.Issue: Could potential claimants to a limited insurance fund be brought into statutory interpleader before their tort claims were adjudicated?
sections.Holding: Yes. The statute’s protection was not confined to persons who already held final judgments.
sections.Reasoning: Waiting for the first claimant to obtain judgment could defeat the purpose of distributing a fund among competing claimants and protecting against inconsistent demands. The statutory reference to persons who may claim supported earlier use. The insurer’s role nevertheless required care: invoking interpleader did not necessarily eliminate every contractual duty owed under the insurance arrangement.

learning.why: The insurer could invoke interpleader before the accident claimants reduced their demands to judgments.

topics.cp-interpleader: Unliquidated accident claims could present competing demands on a limited insurance fund.
topics.cp-statutory-interpleader: The court examined the federal statute’s reach before tort judgments fixed the claims.
topics.cp-frcp-22: The court held that Rule 22 as well as the Interpleader Act allowed interpleader of unliquidated tort claims.
topics.cp-usc-1335: The insurer invoked statutory interpleader and deposited a bond for the policy limit as § 1335 requires.

mnemonic.rationale: A bus crash and a hundred thousand dollars
